class pinn.AdaptiveCache(*, max_memory_mb: int | None = 512, max_items: int | None = None, compression: bool = True, persistent_path: str | Path | None = None, namespace: str = 'default')[source]¶

Memory-aware cache with LRU eviction and optional compression.

Parameters:

  • max_memory_mb – Soft upper bound on memory usage in megabytes. When exceeded the cache evicts low-priority entries until the budget is respected.

  • max_items – Maximum number of items to keep in the cache. None disables the limit.

  • compression – When True cache entries are compressed using gzip and pickled with the highest protocol to reduce memory consumption.

  • persistent_path – Optional path used to persist cache entries with save() and load().

  • namespace – Logical name used when reporting statistics.

class pinn.AdaptiveWeightingConfig(enabled: bool = False, method: str = 'gradnorm', initial_weights: Sequence[float] | None = None, adaptation_rate: float = 0.1, adaptation_frequency: int = 50, history_window: int = 20, uncertainty_window: int = 10, preview_collocation_points: int = 256, temperature: float = 2.0, normalize: bool = True, clip_min: float = 0.001, clip_max: float = 10.0, gradnorm_alpha: float = 1.0, dwa_momentum: float = 0.9, rl_discount: float = 0.95, rl_learning_rate: float = 0.2, rl_epsilon: float = 0.1, bo_exploration: float = 0.25, meta_hidden: int = 64, visualize: bool = True, strict_validation: bool = True, log_history: bool = True)[source]¶

Configuration options for adaptive loss weighting.

Parameters:

  • enabled (bool) – Toggle for enabling adaptive weighting.

  • method (str) – Weighting strategy identifier ("gradnorm", "dwa", "uncertainty", "pareto", "mgda", "meta", "reinforce", "bayes" or "magnitude").

  • initial_weights (Sequence[float] | None) – Optional initial weights per loss component. When None the initial weights are uniform.

  • adaptation_rate (float) – Step size used by strategies that rely on gradient-based updates.

  • adaptation_frequency (int) – Number of optimisation steps between weight updates.

  • history_window (int) – Number of past steps retained for history-based strategies.

  • uncertainty_window (int) – Window size for variance-based (uncertainty) weighting.

  • preview_collocation_points (int) – Number of collocation points used to estimate PDE gradients for gradient-based strategies. Set to 0 to disable previews.

  • temperature (float) – Softmax temperature parameter used by DWA and Bayesian updates.

  • normalize (bool) – If True the weights are normalised to sum to one after each update. Disable to keep absolute scaling but still clamp.

  • clip_min – Lower and upper bounds applied to weights to avoid extreme values.

  • clip_max – Lower and upper bounds applied to weights to avoid extreme values.

  • gradnorm_alpha (float) – Exponent for the GradNorm relative loss term. 1.0 corresponds to the formulation in the original paper.

  • dwa_momentum (float) – Momentum term used to smooth DWA updates.

  • rl_discount – Hyper-parameters controlling the reinforcement-learning-inspired weighting heuristic.

  • rl_learning_rate – Hyper-parameters controlling the reinforcement-learning-inspired weighting heuristic.

  • rl_epsilon – Hyper-parameters controlling the reinforcement-learning-inspired weighting heuristic.

  • meta_hidden (int) – Hidden size for the meta-learning weighting network (used when method is "meta" or "meta_learning").

  • bo_exploration (float) – Exploration factor for the Bayesian weighting heuristic. Higher values encourage sampling more diverse weights.

  • visualize (bool) – Enable weight-history tracking suitable for visualisation.

  • strict_validation (bool) – When True invalid configuration raises ValidationError.

  • log_history (bool) – Toggle for recording per-update history for later inspection.

class pinn.BurgersConfig(tmin: float = 0.0, tmax: float = 1.0, xmin: float = -1.0, xmax: float = 1.0, nu: float = 0.003183098861837907)[source]¶

Configuration for the 1D viscous Burgers equation problem.

Defines the computational domain and physical parameters for the PDE:

class pinn.BurgersProblem(config: BurgersConfig = BurgersConfig(tmin=0.0, tmax=1.0, xmin=-1.0, xmax=1.0, nu=0.003183098861837907), n_constraint_samples: int = 128, reference_quad_points: int = 200)[source]¶

One-dimensional viscous Burgers equation on a space-time rectangle.

The equation is u_t + u u_x - nu u_xx = 0 with the PINN benchmark initial condition u(0, x) = -sin(pi x) and homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries at x = xmin and x = xmax.

class pinn.CacheConfig(enabled: bool = False, identifier: str = 'default', max_memory_mb: int = 512, persistent_path: str | Path | None = None, compression: bool = True, store_samples: bool = True, store_gradients: bool = False, store_losses: bool = False, store_activations: bool = False, refresh_interval: int = 0, async_precompute: bool = False, precompute_workers: int = 2, max_permutation_queue: int = 2, persist_samples: bool = True, lazy_evaluation: bool = True)[source]¶

Configuration options for TrainingCache.

enabled¶

Toggle caching behaviour. When False the TrainingCache becomes a no-op wrapper.

Type:

bool

identifier¶

Logical identifier for cache persistence. When combined with persistent_path this allows training runs to reuse previously saved sampling points.

Type:

str

max_memory_mb¶

Per-cache memory budget applied to each internal AdaptiveCache.

Type:

int

persistent_path¶

Directory used to persist cached artefacts. Files are stored within a cache sub-directory named after identifier.

Type:

str | pathlib.Path | None

compression¶

Enable value compression before storing entries.

Type:

bool

store_samples, store_gradients, store_losses, store_activations

Toggle specialised caches for sampling points, autograd outputs, diagnostic loss values, and forward activations respectively.

refresh_interval¶

Optional number of invocations after which cached sampling points are refreshed (re-generated). 0 disables periodic refreshes.

Type:

int

async_precompute¶

Enable background precomputation utilities for collocation ordering and other expensive transformations.

Type:

bool

precompute_workers¶

Number of worker threads used when async_precompute is enabled.

Type:

int

max_permutation_queue¶

Maximum number of precomputed permutations buffered for reuse.

Type:

int

persist_samples¶

When True cached sampling points are written to disk for reuse in future runs.

Type:

bool

lazy_evaluation¶

Enable memoisation helpers to lazily compute expensive functions.

bool

class pinn.ContinuousPINN(model: Module, device: str | device, pde_residual_fn: Callable[[Module, Tensor, Tensor, float], Tensor], cfg_burgers: BurgersConfig)[source]¶

Physics-Informed Neural Network for continuous-time PDE solving.

This class implements the standard PINN approach where the PDE residual is enforced at collocation points throughout the domain, while initial and boundary conditions are enforced through supervised learning.

model¶

Neural network model

device¶

Computation device (CPU or CUDA)

cfg¶

Problem configuration

pde_residual_fn¶

Function to compute PDE residuals

loss_history¶

Dictionary tracking loss components during training

Dictionary with loss component names as keys and loss values as lists

loss_history: Dict[str, List[float]]¶

Predict solution values at given (t, x) points.

Parameters:

  • t – Time coordinates, must have same shape as x

  • x – Spatial coordinates, must have same shape as t

  • batch_size – Batch size for prediction to manage memory

Returns:

Predicted solution values with same shape as input arrays

Raises:

ValueError – If t and x don’t have the same shape

train(tcfg: TrainConfig, weights: Tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0), checkpoint_manager: CheckpointManager | None = None, resume: bool = False, *, callbacks: Iterable[Callable[[int, Dict[str, float]], None]] | None = None, distributed: Any | None = None) → Dict[str, List[float]][source]¶

Train the PINN using Adam optimizer and optional L-BFGS polish.

The training loop is augmented with gradient accumulation, mixed precision, and memory monitoring utilities so that large collocation sets can be handled efficiently without exhausting device memory.

class pinn.GradientBasedImportanceSampler(domain: Domain, base_sampler: BaseSampler, *, update_frequency: int = 100, n_candidates: int = 1024, strategy: str = 'gradient', device: device | str | None = None)[source]¶

Adaptive sampler that biases points based on loss gradients.

Parameters:

  • domain – Sampling domain describing the bounds of each dimension.

  • base_sampler – Sampler used to draw candidate points (e.g. LatinHypercubeSampler).

  • update_frequency – Number of sample calls between importance weight updates.

  • n_candidates – Number of candidate points used to estimate the importance map. The larger this value the smoother the distribution but also the more expensive the update.

  • strategy – Importance metric to use. "gradient" uses the gradient magnitude of the provided loss function w.r.t. the inputs. "residual" expects the loss function to return residual values directly. "error" uses the absolute error returned by the loss function.

  • device – Optional torch device for gradient computations. If None the device is inferred from the model when sample is called.

importance_map() → tuple[Tensor, Tensor] | None[source]¶

Return the last points and their associated weights.

property importance_weights: Tensor | None¶
property last_points: Tensor | None¶
sample(n_points: int, *, model: Module | None = None, loss_fn: Callable[[Module, Tensor], Tensor] | None = None) → Tensor[source]¶

Draw n_points samples from the current importance distribution.

If called before any importance map has been computed or if the update frequency has been reached, the importance weights are recomputed using model and loss_fn.

class pinn.NavierStokesPINN(model: Module, cfg: NSConfig, device: str | device = 'cpu')[source]¶

Physics-Informed Neural Network for 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes (u,v,p). Enforces:

  • Momentum x/y residuals

  • Continuity (divergence-free)

  • Initial condition (from Taylor–Green vortex by default)

  • Periodic boundary conditions (loss on paired samples at opposite faces)

class pinn.Trainer(config: TrainerConfig | None = None, *, derivative_backend: DerivativeBackend | None = None, residual_form: StrongFormResidual | None = None)[source]¶

Generic trainer for PDEProblem instances.

The trainer knows how to combine residual and constraint losses, but it does not know which equation is being solved. Equation-specific work belongs to the problem, residual form and constraints.

train(problem: PDEProblem, model: Module) → TrainingResult[source]¶

Train model on problem and return recorded state history.

class pinn.TrainerConfig(seed: int = 0, device: str | device = 'cpu', dtype: dtype | str = torch.float32, collocation_count: int = 1000, sampler: InteriorSampler = <factory>, constraint_sample_counts: Mapping[str, int]=<factory>, optimizer: OptimizerConfig = <factory>, log_every: int = 100, loss_weights: Mapping[str, float]=<factory>, causal: CausalWeightConfig | None = None, scaling: Nondimensionalizer | None = None, adaptive_refinement: ResidualAdaptiveConfig | None = None)[source]¶

Configuration for equation-agnostic PINN training.

Parameters:

  • seed – Random seed propagated to Python, NumPy and PyTorch.

  • device – Torch device used for model and sampled tensors.

  • dtype – Floating-point dtype for the new core path.

  • collocation_count – Number of interior residual points.

  • sampler – Interior sampler used for trainer-owned residual points.

  • constraint_sample_counts – Optional per-constraint sample-count overrides.

  • optimizer – Adam and optional L-BFGS settings.

  • log_every – Record loss diagnostics every this many Adam steps.

  • loss_weights – Optional per-loss weights keyed by "pde" or a constraint name.

  • causal – Optional causal residual weighting configuration.

  • scaling – Optional physical nondimensionalization transform. When set, the raw model is trained in dimensionless input/output variables while problems and constraints still see dimensional values.

  • adaptive_refinement – Optional residual-based adaptive refinement configuration for adding high-residual collocation points. The refiner can optionally weight coordinate diversity during candidate selection.

Advanced PINN architectures.

This module collects several neural network architectures that extend the basic MLP model with additional capabilities tailored for challenging PDE problems. The implementations are lightweight and focus on demonstrating the interfaces required for experimentation rather than being state of the art. Each model is fully differentiable and can be composed with standard training loops.

class pinn.training.AdaptiveWeightingConfig(enabled: bool = False, method: str = 'gradnorm', initial_weights: Sequence[float] | None = None, adaptation_rate: float = 0.1, adaptation_frequency: int = 50, history_window: int = 20, uncertainty_window: int = 10, preview_collocation_points: int = 256, temperature: float = 2.0, normalize: bool = True, clip_min: float = 0.001, clip_max: float = 10.0, gradnorm_alpha: float = 1.0, dwa_momentum: float = 0.9, rl_discount: float = 0.95, rl_learning_rate: float = 0.2, rl_epsilon: float = 0.1, bo_exploration: float = 0.25, meta_hidden: int = 64, visualize: bool = True, strict_validation: bool = True, log_history: bool = True)[source]¶

Configuration options for adaptive loss weighting.

Parameters:

  • enabled (bool) – Toggle for enabling adaptive weighting.

  • method (str) – Weighting strategy identifier ("gradnorm", "dwa", "uncertainty", "pareto", "mgda", "meta", "reinforce", "bayes" or "magnitude").

  • initial_weights (Sequence[float] | None) – Optional initial weights per loss component. When None the initial weights are uniform.

  • adaptation_rate (float) – Step size used by strategies that rely on gradient-based updates.

  • adaptation_frequency (int) – Number of optimisation steps between weight updates.

  • history_window (int) – Number of past steps retained for history-based strategies.

  • uncertainty_window (int) – Window size for variance-based (uncertainty) weighting.

  • preview_collocation_points (int) – Number of collocation points used to estimate PDE gradients for gradient-based strategies. Set to 0 to disable previews.

  • temperature (float) – Softmax temperature parameter used by DWA and Bayesian updates.

  • normalize (bool) – If True the weights are normalised to sum to one after each update. Disable to keep absolute scaling but still clamp.

  • clip_min – Lower and upper bounds applied to weights to avoid extreme values.

  • clip_max – Lower and upper bounds applied to weights to avoid extreme values.

  • gradnorm_alpha (float) – Exponent for the GradNorm relative loss term. 1.0 corresponds to the formulation in the original paper.

  • dwa_momentum (float) – Momentum term used to smooth DWA updates.

  • rl_discount – Hyper-parameters controlling the reinforcement-learning-inspired weighting heuristic.

  • rl_learning_rate – Hyper-parameters controlling the reinforcement-learning-inspired weighting heuristic.

  • rl_epsilon – Hyper-parameters controlling the reinforcement-learning-inspired weighting heuristic.

  • meta_hidden (int) – Hidden size for the meta-learning weighting network (used when method is "meta" or "meta_learning").

  • bo_exploration (float) – Exploration factor for the Bayesian weighting heuristic. Higher values encourage sampling more diverse weights.

  • visualize (bool) – Enable weight-history tracking suitable for visualisation.

  • strict_validation (bool) – When True invalid configuration raises ValidationError.

  • log_history (bool) – Toggle for recording per-update history for later inspection.

class pinn.training.CausalWeightConfig(enabled: bool = True, n_chunks: int = 16, eps: float = 1.0, tol: float = 0.99)[source]¶

Settings for causal residual weighting.

enabled¶

Whether to apply causal weighting at all.

Type:

bool

n_chunks¶

Number of consecutive time windows the interval is split into.

Type:

int

eps¶

Causality parameter. Larger values enforce the temporal ordering more strictly; as it approaches zero the loss becomes the ordinary unweighted mean.

Type:

float

tol¶

Convergence criterion. Training on the whole interval can be considered complete once the smallest weight exceeds this value, meaning even the last window is being optimised.

Type:

float

pinn.training.causal_residual_loss(residual: Tensor, t: Tensor, config: CausalWeightConfig, tmin: float, tmax: float) → Tuple[Tensor, Tensor][source]¶

Reduce a pointwise PDE residual to a causally weighted scalar loss.

Parameters:

  • residual – Pointwise residual, shape (N,) or (N, 1).

  • t – Matching time coordinates, shape (N,) or (N, 1).

  • config – Causal weighting settings.

  • tmin – Start of the time interval.

  • tmax – End of the time interval.

Returns:

A tuple of the scalar loss and the per-window weights. When weighting is disabled the loss is the plain mean squared residual and the returned weights are all ones.

Raises:

ValueError – If the configuration is invalid or the shapes disagree.

pinn.training.causal_weights(chunk_losses: Tensor, eps: float) → Tensor[source]¶

Compute the causal weight of each time window.

Parameters:

  • chunk_losses – Mean residual per window, shape (M,), ordered by time.

  • eps – Causality parameter.

Returns:

Weights of shape (M,), detached from the graph. The first window always has weight 1, and each later one decays with the accumulated residual of everything before it.

pinn.visualization.export_animation(fig: Figure, path: str) → None[source]¶

Export fig with animation frames to path.
